title: Ashmita Chaliha Wins Korea Masters, Secures Maiden BWF World Tour Title
indian_angle: Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha achieved a significant milestone by winning her first BWF World Tour title, marking a strong comeback for Indian badminton.
summary: The 26-year-old Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha clinched the Korea Masters, her maiden BWF World Tour title, completing an impressive return after a serious knee injury suffered in 2024.

title: Ashmita Chaliha Joins Elite Indian Women's Badminton Club After Korea Masters Triumph
indian_angle: Ashmita Chaliha's victory places her among an exclusive group of Indian women, becoming only the fifth to win a Super 300 or higher BWF title.
summary: Following her Korea Masters triumph, Ashmita Chaliha has entered an exclusive club as only the fifth Indian woman to win a Super 300 or higher BWF title, alongside Saina Nehwal, PV Sindhu, Devika Sihag, and Tanvi Sharma.

title: Indian Badminton Coach Park Tae-Sang Reaping Rewards of Hard Work
indian_angle: Coach Park Tae-Sang's dedicated efforts are yielding positive results for Indian badminton, nurturing the next generation of stars.
summary: Coach Park Tae-Sang's long-term commitment to developing Indian badminton players is now evident through recent good results, hinting at a promising future for the sport in the country.

title: From Olympic Bronze to Super 300s: Park Tae-Sang's Next Act Takes Shape
indian_angle: After guiding PV Sindhu to Olympic bronze, coach Park Tae-Sang is now focused on developing a new wave of Indian talent, with recent successes highlighting his impact.
summary: Following his success with PV Sindhu, coach Park Tae-Sang is now focused on building the next generation of Indian badminton stars, with recent back-to-back Super 300 victories highlighting his impact.
